referee_note: Five reviewer slots: R1, R3, R4 wrote reports; R2 and R5 are early-career co-reviewers with no separate comments. R1 is signed (Ramos-Alonso and Ochoa, Columbia) in round 2. Round 2 (Version 1): R1, R3 comments, R4 no further comments. Round 3 (Version 2): R3 recommends publication with no new concerns. Journal: Nature Communications.
match_note: First-round reports cite features that match v1 exactly: Fig. 2 built from three TBG devices (2 deg, MATBG1 1.05 deg, MATBG2 1.04 deg) with monolayer panel 2f plotted as normalized percentage; Fig. 2b non-monotonic power dependence near full filling; Fig. 2e TL dependence; Fig. 3 on the 1.58 deg device; 0.14 THz source; 'Te up to 15 K above the cold lattice'; theory building on Ref. 43 with Lambda spanning 0.01-1. Device nomenclature (MATBG1/2) was renamed only in revision. The v1 PDF does not include the SI, so concerns about SI figures (S4, S5, S8, S9) are marked in_v1 false or noted.

concerns.quote: their interpretation of the photoresistance data assumes that THz radiation "selectively heats the electronic system"; this is an assumption that cannot be deduced from the data.
concerns.summary: The claim that THz light heats only electrons and leaves the lattice cold is assumed, not shown, and TBG has strong electron-phonon coupling (Birkbeck et al.), so a phonon-dominated resistivity is not excluded.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis
concerns.response_detail: Authors added a graphite-heater vs DC-heating thermal experiment (lattice overheating bound below 1 K) and Johnson noise thermometry.

concerns.quote: The exclusion of electron-phonon scattering from the THz photoresponse is plausible but not rigorously demonstrated. ... the monolayer graphene control may not represent the enhanced e-ph coupling in TBG
concerns.summary: A positive photoresistance shows electron interactions matter but does not prove the phonon contribution is negligible; the monolayer graphene control does not capture TBG's enhanced coupling, and a quantitative e-ph estimate is missing.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis
concerns.response_detail: Bloch-Gruneisen kinematic argument plus a new lattice-temperature slope analysis (Figs R10/R11) bounding the phonon slope; R3 and R1 stayed partly unconvinced in round 2.

concerns.quote: We don't understand how electrons can thermalize upon illumination if they are essentially decoupled from the lattice. For the same reasons, it's unclear to us how the electronic system can relax again to the light-off state.
concerns.summary: The paper gives no physical picture of the light-on steady state or of how hot electrons relax if they are decoupled from the lattice.
concerns.response_detail: Heat-balance model (Wiedemann-Franz and acoustic phonon emission, out-of-plane sinking) added to SI; supported by the new thermal data.

concerns.quote: It is unclear, for example, in how many devices they observed the effect. ... the conclusions would be on a more solid foundation if all the statements in the text were supported from observations in a single device
concerns.summary: The number of devices is not stated, different devices illustrate different aspects (even within Fig. 2), and reproducibility across devices, including power dependence, is not shown; a summary table is requested.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis
concerns.response_detail: Device table added (10 TBG devices, 6 with THz antennas) and cross-device comparison in SI Secs VI-XII; R3 still preferred single-device demonstration.

concerns.quote: interpreted as the resistivity of the material in the absence of the light beam, but at a higher temperature. However, this is only explicitly shown from the data of one of the devices
concerns.summary: The mapping of photoresistance onto an equivalent electron temperature is shown for only one device.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis
concerns.response_detail: Te estimates added for TBG1.04 and TBG2.0 (Fig R8).
concerns.in_v1_note: The 15 K electron overheating claim is in v1 main text; the one-device calibration figure is SI, not in the v1 PDF.

concerns.quote: the longitudinal (four terminal?) resistance
concerns.summary: It is not stated whether the longitudinal resistance is measured in a four-terminal configuration.
concerns.response_detail: Authors state measurements are four-terminal (in reply to R4).

concerns.quote: the theory has very little predictive power: The obtained resistivity is found to be proportional to a parameter whose value can expand over two orders of magnitude.
concerns.summary: The intervalley T^2 resistivity prediction depends on a parameter Lambda that spans 0.01 to 1, so it barely constrains the data.
concerns.response_detail: Acknowledged the uncertainty; argued gate screening dominates and the mechanism is the only known Fermi-liquid route away from the magic angle.

concerns.quote: the theory provides an answer for a question that is not posed by the experimental data ... there is no experimental evidence that the resistivity is dominated by electron-electron scattering at those carrier concentrations
concerns.summary: The theory explains interaction-limited T^2 resistivity at very low and very high densities, where the photoresistance data do not show interaction-dominated transport.
concerns.response_detail: Argued T^2 near the CNP itself signals e-e scattering and pointed to positive photoresistance in TBG2.0; R1 repeated the objection in its round 2 summary.

concerns.quote: Can the authors provide an explanation for why the photoresistance of Fig. 2b around n=±2.6e12 cm^-2 behaves differently as a function of light intensity ... why does the photoresistance become first positive and then negative
concerns.summary: Near full filling the photoresistance is non-monotonic in light power, which contradicts the electron-heating interpretation.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis
concerns.response_detail: Authors called it a lock-in out-of-phase artifact in highly resistive devices and showed monotonic behaviour in TBG1.04 (Fig R5).

concerns.quote: Note also how fillings above/below +/- 3.5 are excluded from the analysis in Fig. S8 of the SI.
concerns.summary: Fillings beyond +/-3.5 are left out of the electron-temperature analysis, where the data deviate from the interpretation.
concerns.response_detail: Justified as focus on the metallic regime; SI expanded.
concerns.in_v1_note: Concerns an SI figure not in the v1 PDF.

concerns.quote: note that the photoresistance close to neutrality in TBG (see Fig. S9a in the SI) are of the same order (in percentage) as in monolayer graphene (Fig. 2f).
concerns.summary: Near neutrality the TBG photoresistance is no larger in percentage terms than the monolayer control, undercutting the contrast.
concerns.response_detail: Authors disagreed, calling it a comparison of different transport regimes.
concerns.in_v1_note: Compares SI Fig S9a (not in v1 PDF) with v1 Fig 2f.

concerns.quote: for these two devices, the resistivity (with no radiation) as a function of temperature saturates ... Necessarily, the photoresistance must decrease with temperature. That would be also the case if the lattice was warmed up together with electrons
concerns.summary: The fade of photoresistance with lattice temperature (Fig. 2e) follows trivially from saturating dark resistivity and does not support electron-only heating or any cooling mechanism; is it seen at larger twist angles?
concerns.response_detail: Round 1 reply gave a heat-balance argument and Te(TL) fits but did not answer the saturation point; addressed with dρ/dT data only in round 2.

concerns.quote: Is the frequency of light for the data in Fig. 2f (monolayer graphene) the same as the one used for the twisted devices? More importantly, what is the intensity of light in the monolayer case?
concerns.summary: The monolayer graphene control's THz frequency and intensity are not given, so it may not be comparable to the TBG measurements.
concerns.response_detail: Stated MLG used 0.69 THz at similar output power.

concerns.quote: Please consider plotting Δρ_THz/ρ so that datasets from different devices with different base resistivities, geometries, or light coupling efficiencies are directly comparable
concerns.summary: Photoresistance units are inconsistent (percent for monolayer, ohms for TBG) and should be normalized for cross-device comparison.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis
concerns.response_detail: All data converted to ohms; normalized Δρ/ρ0 plots added to SI, with argument that ρ0 normalization is not physically meaningful.

concerns.quote: the manuscript discusses the photo response across different twist angles but does not quantify how its magnitude varies systematically.
concerns.summary: The twist-angle dependence of the relative photoresistance at fixed filling is not quantified.
concerns.response_detail: Showed Δρ/ρ0 for several devices and a table of maxima, but declined a quantitative cross-device comparison as beyond scope.

concerns.quote: Does the photoresistance depend on the modulation frequency of the incident light power?
concerns.summary: Dependence on the light modulation frequency is not reported.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis
concerns.response_detail: New data (Fig R6) show insensitivity over 44-121 Hz.

concerns.quote: if the resistance can be really thought as a step-like function of time, the n-th harmonic should be also proportional to the photoresistance, but a factor 1/n smaller. Is that the case?
concerns.summary: The step-like resistance model predicts higher harmonics scaling as 1/n, which is not checked.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis
concerns.response_detail: New data (Fig R7) follow the predicted odd-harmonic 1/n scaling.

concerns.quote: The angle determination for higher-angle devices lacks clear experimental confirmation (no superlattice peaks observed), so the actual twist angle may differ from the mentioned value.
concerns.summary: Twist angles of the larger-angle devices are not experimentally confirmed and their uncertainty is not discussed.
concerns.response_detail: Explained Brown-Zak oscillations for 2.2 deg, stacking targets with 0.1-0.2 deg relaxation, and effective-mass checks.

concerns.quote: Figure 3 shows an extended region of T-linear resistivity at intermediate fillings in the 1.58° TBG device, yet the discussion focuses solely on the T^2 regimes. Please clarify the microscopic origin
concerns.summary: The T-linear regime at intermediate fillings in the 1.58 deg device is not explained.
concerns.response_detail: Declined a definitive claim; suggested a van Hove singularity marginal-Fermi-liquid scenario.

concerns.quote: At these twist angles, the moiré coupling is weak and the two layers should behave nearly as independent monolayer graphene sheets, where T-linear behavior is typically phonon-driven.
concerns.summary: T-linear resistivity in the 2.2 and 2.7 deg devices is more naturally phonon-driven, so attributing it to interactions is not justified.
concerns.response_detail: Argued slope exceeds monolayer values and added a phonon-slope analysis, but only on near-magic-angle devices; in round 2 the authors conceded no THz data exist for these devices and narrowed claims.
concerns.in_v1_note: The claim about larger-angle devices is in v1 text; the specific S4c-d figures are SI.

concerns.quote: The manuscript presents all THz-photoresponse data at a single frequency (0.14 THz). Have you checked whether the observed photoresistance is frequency-independent, or could it be influenced by resonant or rectification effects?
concerns.summary: Only one THz frequency is used, so resonant or rectification effects are not excluded.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis
concerns.response_detail: New data at 2.5 and 3.5 THz plus argument that dual modulation removes rectified photovoltage.

concerns.quote: If feasible, a direct measurement of the electron temperature ... would greatly strengthen the interpretation of the THz heating mechanism.
concerns.summary: A direct electron-temperature measurement such as Johnson noise thermometry would test the heating picture.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis
concerns.response_detail: Johnson noise thermometry performed on a separate sub-1 deg device.

concerns.quote: The manuscript discusses THz power in normalized units. For a complete better understanding of the hot-electron effect, please specify the exact power or fluence.
concerns.summary: Absolute THz power or fluence is not given.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis
concerns.response_detail: Pyroelectric beam-profile calibration (incident about 100 uW) and absorbed-power estimate (10-100 nW) added.

concerns.quote: The authors should explain why they think the signal originates only from the graphene channel and not from any artifacts arising from the illumination of the the contacts.
concerns.summary: The THz beam is far larger than the device, so contact illumination could produce artifacts.
concerns.response_detail: Argued four-terminal geometry and dual modulation exclude contact effects; beam size about 2 cm stated.

concerns.quote: Why is it that, though the filling factor varies a lot from +4 to -4, the final electronic temperature increase is the same 13 K (e.g., Figure S8a)?
concerns.summary: The extracted electron temperature rise is implausibly independent of filling even though absorption, heat capacity and cooling should vary.
concerns.response_detail: Authors admitted no definitive explanation and said the behaviour is not reproduced in TBG2.0.
concerns.in_v1_note: Concerns an SI figure not in the v1 PDF.

later_concerns.quote: New low-energy branches appear in the THz domain, and many of them are infrared-active due to the inhomogenous distribution of charge within the moiré pattern when the system is charged.
later_concerns.summary: THz light may couple directly to infrared-active moiré phonons (phasons), so the electron-only absorption hypothesis is unsupported.
later_concerns.response_detail: Acknowledged and cited; argued the thermal-sinking bound limits lattice heating whatever the absorption pathway.

later_concerns.quote: Does figure R4b in the response imply that electrons are heated, or that only electrons are heated? We believe it is proof of the former only.
later_concerns.summary: Johnson noise data show electrons are heated, not that only electrons are heated.
later_concerns.response_detail: Agreed; relied on the thermal bound and nonlinear Te(P).

later_concerns.quote: In moirés, some of the aforementioned low-energy phonon modes are incoherent (diffusive phasons) and can give rise to T2-resistivity followed by an extended linear-in-T regime
later_concerns.summary: Electron-phason scattering can give T^2 and extended T-linear resistivity, contradicting the claim that no phonon mechanism yields T^2.
later_concerns.response_detail: Toned down claims and added references.

later_concerns.quote: if the dark resistivity gradually ceases to be a function of temperature, then this behavior is to be expected and cannot be taken as evidence of any specific cooling or transport mechanism.
later_concerns.summary: The fade of photoresistance with lattice temperature is still explained by saturating dark resistivity; dark and photo data for TBG2.0 should cover the same temperature range.
later_concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis
later_concerns.response_detail: Showed dρ/dT stays large where photoresistance has vanished and extended TBG2.0 dark data to 180 K.

later_concerns.quote: this is a mischaracterization of the behavior of TBG2.0 (Fig. S7 c and d), which displays a significant dependence on band fillings ... the behavior with TL is in fact non-monotonic.
later_concerns.summary: In the ~2 deg device the photoresistance decay is filling dependent, non-monotonic and survives to high temperature, contrary to the stated universal behaviour.
later_concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis
later_concerns.response_detail: Corrected SI text; explained non-monotonicity via Te(TL) combined with dρ/dT and showed Te-TL decays monotonically.

later_concerns.quote: we don't think there is enough evidence to claim that the resistivity is interaction-dominated beyond the magic-angle regime.
later_concerns.summary: Claims of interaction-dominated resistivity beyond the magic angle should be toned down.
later_concerns.response_detail: Reworded to 'significant contribution' for high-angle devices.

later_concerns.quote: the conclusions regarding interaction-dominated transport across different twist-angle regimes rely on comparisons between different devices and indirect arguments
later_concerns.summary: Cross-regime conclusions rest on different devices and indirect arguments.

later_concerns.quote: a significant portion of the analysis ... is focused on the T² regime, where the THz-based approach does not play a direct role
later_concerns.summary: The T^2 analysis in Fig. 3 does not use the THz method, fragmenting the narrative.
later_concerns.response_detail: Argued it is a natural complement.

later_concerns.quote: it is now clear from the summary table that photoresponse measurements were not performed on the 2.2° and 2.7° devices.
later_concerns.summary: No THz data exist for the 2.2 and 2.7 deg devices, so their T-linear resistivity cannot be attributed to interactions.
later_concerns.response_detail: Conceded and narrowed claims to devices with THz data.

later_concerns.quote: the comparison between ρ_THz(T_L) and equilibrium ρ(T_L) in Fig. R10 appears to be made over different temperature ranges (2–4 K vs up to ~20 K)
later_concerns.summary: The phonon-slope comparison uses mismatched temperature windows over non-linear ρ(T).
later_concerns.response_detail: Added low-T fits and argued the mismatch is physically motivated.

later_concerns.quote: This raises the question of to what extent the use of THz excitation is essential to the central conclusions, as opposed to the broader hot-electron framework.
later_concerns.summary: Joule heating gives similar conclusions, so the necessity of THz excitation is unclear.
later_concerns.response_detail: Argued isotropic distribution and practical advantages.

later_concerns.quote: it would be more informative to include a similar comparison in the metallic regime, where the main conclusions are drawn.
later_concerns.summary: Frequency comparison is shown only near the correlated insulator, not in the metallic regime.
later_concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis
later_concerns.response_detail: Added metallic-regime frequency comparison to SI.

later_concerns.quote: the assumption that T_BG scales simply with k_F may be less straightforward in TBG due to the modified band structure
later_concerns.summary: The Bloch-Gruneisen scaling argument used to exclude phonons may not hold in TBG.
later_concerns.response_detail: Cited Das Sarma group work placing T_BG at a few K.

first_round.quote: We cannot recommend the publication of the manuscript in its current form... However, the authors should be given the opportunity to address our concerns and improve the presentation of the data.
I co-reviewed this manuscript with one of the reviewers who provided the listed reports.
many of the quantitative and interpretative aspects could be improved. I suggest addressing following points
the reviewer recommends the publication of this work provided the authors can address the following concerns.
I co-reviewed this manuscript with one of the reviewers who provided the listed reports.

recommendations.note: First round is Version 0. The file shows no sign of a transfer from another journal. R2 and R5 are Early Career co-reviewers who wrote no independent assessment, and neither says which referee they worked with. R2 is assigned R1's recommendation because it directly follows R1 and R1's round-2 report is signed by two people (Ramos-Alonso and Ochoa); this is still an inference. R5's pairing is uncertain: it is assigned R4's recommendation only because it directly follows R4, but it could instead belong with R3 (major revision). R3 gives no explicit verdict in round 1. It was classed as major revision because it requests substantial new analysis: a quantitative e-ph estimate, cross-device comparison tables, normalized plots, and optionally data at other frequencies and noise thermometry. Its positive tone means minor revision is also arguable. R4 conditionally recommends publication with a set of concerns to address, so it was classed as minor revision.
recommendations.label: contested
